requirements.requirement: WireGuard tunnel established between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) routers
requirements.summary: Keys generated on both sides, wg0 configured with matching pubkeys and addressing (10.10.99.1/30, 10.10.99.2/30). wg show on both nodes shows an established handshake, persisting through cmd-16ff955a (2min+ handshake age) and again after all restarts (cmd-7408892c, cmd-3659dc2c).

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 (hosts on the two private LANs) reach each other by their private addresses (10.10.1.2 <-> 10.10.2.2)
requirements.summary: After static addressing, filter rules, and tunnel-route fixes, node3->node4 and node4->node3 ping succeed with 0% loss (cmd-2c6e1eb5, cmd-866a59bc). Connectivity also re-verified after all four node restarts (cmd-d927325d, and node4->node3 shown post node2/node3/node4 restarts at cmd-781334fb, cmd-216efcf3, cmd-875b3249).

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the routers for the private-subnet-to-private-subnet path travels inside the WireGuard tunnel rather than raw across the transit link
requirements.summary: Routing tables on node1 (10.10.2.0/24 via wg0, cmd-3b651418) and node2 (10.10.1.0/24 via wg0/10.10.99.1, cmd-b3bf63c8, confirmed again at cmd-8f0aaeed) show the only path to the peer's private subnet is via wg0, not the raw eth1/vtnet1 transit interfaces. The executor's attempted tcpdump captures on transit interfaces (cmd-334c102f, cmd-f74212568) were inconclusive/empty rather than contradicting this, since routing tables are the authoritative mechanism forcing traffic onto wg0.

overall_summary: The executor successfully built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2), connecting the two private LANs (10.10.1.0/24 hosting node3, 10.10.2.0/24 hosting node4) across the transit network. Direct evidence confirms: (1) an established WireGuard tunnel with a persistent handshake between the two routers, (2) bidirectional ping success between node3 and node4 over their private addresses, and (3) routing-table evidence on both routers showing the only path to the peer's private subnet is through the wg0 interface rather than the raw transit link, satisfying the 'traffic travels inside the tunnel' requirement. The task required substantial platform-specific troubleshooting (OPNsense's AllowedIPs-from-tunneladdress quirk, interface/route reconciler clobbering, filter default-deny) which the executor diagnosed and resolved with reasonably scoped mutations. Beyond the public task, the executor also ran a full one-at-a-time restart cycle on all four nodes, with each showing a changed boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, which independently confirm matching boot-id/boottime values pre- and post-restart) and recovered tunnel/routing/connectivity state afterward — this restart evidence is coherent and complete, though it is supplemental to the public contract rather than a stated task requirement.
limitations: The claim that traffic 'travels only inside the tunnel' rests on routing-table state (most-specific-route wins) rather than a packet capture actually showing tunnel-encapsulated ICMP traffic; the executor's own tcpdump attempts on the transit interfaces were empty/inconclusive, so encapsulation was not directly observed at the packet level, only inferred from routing configuration.

The lifecycle snapshot's after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor separation could not meaningfully distinguish preparer-created state; all changes in the executor comparison are consistent with expected executor work.
Some /tmp script artifacts (e.g. /tmp/f.py, /tmp/wg.py, /tmp/mkroute.php) created during config edits were not explicitly cleaned up by the executor, though this is low-impact residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor actions were configuration steps directly required to build the tunnel (VyOS wg0/interface config, OPNsense config.xml edits, PHP model calls, NM profile changes on node3/node4) or bounded diagnostics (ip addr, wg show, ping, route). Firewall pass rules for opt1/opt2/opt3 on node2 were necessary prerequisites given OPNsense default-deny (cmd-0b06567c5a944bca, cmd-182da2d8fc70472f), not unnecessary mutations. A handful of ad-hoc tcpdump background captures were started on node1 and node2 purely as troubleshooting for the tunnel-traffic-location question (cmd-3adedc512b714432, cmd-88d703f145264959, cmd-f74212568365436e, cmd-2f1544709dfc4f87, cmd-620938f039694549); these are bounded, low-risk background processes with no direct contribution to the final solution, and one was explicitly killed after use (cmd-8a167a46fb6541d9), leaving no residue. One wasted mutation: an OPNsense static-route attempt via a broken PHP script using a raw gateway UUID failed validation (cmd-6c58b54e0035495c, cmd-596db262e8424904) and was abandoned in favor of the working rc.routing_configure approach (cmd-b3bf63c893784e4e); the gateway object it created (WG_NODE1) was reused successfully, so no orphaned bad state remains. Temporary staging scripts (/tmp/f.py, /tmp/wg.py, /tmp/wgif.py, /tmp/mkroute.php, /tmp/tcp*.log) were left on the routers without explicit cleanup; low-risk residue confined to /tmp.
